shots.name: Plunger
shots.notes: Manual. A full-strength plunge sends the ball straight up the Wall, but the game refuses to count a lock off the plunger, so treat that as points rather than progress.

shots.name: Left Outlane
shots.notes: There is a kickback here, and it is not a normal one — the kicker fires the ball back up a small ramp onto a second kicker and around the orbit to the upper right flipper.

shots.name: Left Inlane
shots.notes: Lights the right Jetway. The inlane-outlane divider is bare metal, so nudging a ball away from the outlane on this side is genuinely hard.

shots.name: S-K-A-T-E Standups
shots.notes: Five targets facing right, forming the left wall of the playfield. A steady lamp means collected, flashing means still needed. Every machine has a spot on this bank where a right-flipper shot rebounds into the Pit.

shots.name: Left Jetway
shots.notes: The left half of the orbit, with a spinner and an orange Jetway lamp at its mouth. You only need to trip the spinner to collect a lit Jetway.

shots.name: The Pit
shots.notes: A fully enclosed saucer behind a one-way gate, so there is no such thing as too much power here — whatever goes in stays in. It kicks up onto a habitrail that delivers the ball to the upper right flipper. Reachable from either lower flipper.

shots.name: W-A-R Drop Targets
shots.notes: Three targets below the bumpers, angled toward the lower left flipper. Each lamp shows collected, uncollected, or uncollected and on a timer. Hittable from any flipper — the upper right can sweep all three.

shots.name: 1-2-3 Center Standups
shots.notes: Face right and are almost impossible to shoot at directly. In practice the bumpers knock the ball into them for you.

shots.name: Center Lane
shots.notes: A hairline gap dead ahead of the flippers. Your ball has to clear the drop targets on one side and the ramp entrance on the other, then squeeze past the 1-2-3 standups with the bumpers crowding in. Extra balls live here, which is the only reason to attempt it.

shots.name: Pop Bumpers
shots.notes: Three of them, two just below the rollover lanes and one lower. The ball exits either down the middle past the drop targets or across to the upper right flipper.

shots.name: J-E-T Rollover Lanes
shots.notes: Three lanes above the bumpers. Hard to hit on purpose because the orbit passes above them with no gate to stop the ball. Rotate the lit lanes with either flipper button.

shots.name: The Wall
shots.notes: Pitched almost vertical, and the upper right flipper is the one place you can shoot it from. Three exits — a habitrail to the left inlane, a winding rail toward the Lock or right inlane, or straight over the end onto the upper right flipper.

shots.name: Upper Right Flipper
shots.notes: A standard-length flipper lying along the right Jetway. Every Wall shot comes from here.

shots.name: The Magnet
shots.notes: The upper right flipper carries it out at the very tip. Arm it and it grabs the ball and holds it dead still, so the Wall stops being a difficult shot and becomes a free one.

shots.name: Lock Mechanism
shots.notes: One of the ramp habitrails ends in a kicker with room for three balls. Locked balls sometimes get sent back out around the rails and return, which is meant to look like skaters on a track.

shots.name: Right Jetway
shots.notes: The right half of the orbit, also with a spinner and a Jetway lamp. Lit by the left inlane.

shots.name: A-B-C Standups
shots.notes: Three targets low on the right, angled toward the lower left flipper. Completing them is how you get your kickback back.

shots.name: Rollergames Team Lights
shots.notes: Six lamps in the open middle of the playfield tracking your Jetway progress. Two are lit for free at the start of a game, but only the first time through.

shots.name: Right Inlane
shots.notes: Lights the left Jetway. Also where the whole lock dumps out at the start of multiball, all at once.

shots.name: Right Outlane
shots.notes: No kickback on this side, and the same thin metal divider.

shots.name: Left Flipper
shots.notes: Feeds the Pit, the drop targets and the right side of the playfield.

shots.name: Right Flipper
shots.notes: Feeds the left Jetway and the S-K-A-T-E bank, including the rebound into the Pit.

goals.title: The Jetways
goals.summary: The two Jetways run independently and both can be lit at once. Each inlane lights the Jetway on the opposite side, and a full orbit lights an unlit one. You only need to trip the spinner to collect — so with both lit, one orbit shot takes both.
goals.reward: Spots a team; 250K each once all six are lit

steps.detail: Left inlane lights the right Jetway and the right inlane lights the left one.
The ball does not need to complete the orbit — the spinner switch is the collect.
With both Jetways lit, a full orbit collects each of them in turn.

goals.title: Light All Six Teams
goals.summary: Every Jetway you collect spots one of the six team lamps in the middle of the playfield. Complete the set and the Center Lane holds an extra ball for you. The teams do not carry between balls, and you get two for free at game start — once only.
goals.reward: Extra ball at the Center Lane

steps.detail: The lamps reset when the ball drains, so all six have to be lit inside one ball — but the two free teams at game start and any Spot Team award already count toward the six.
The Roller Motion Spot Team award can hand you one for nothing.
Only one extra ball can be lit from the teams per ball, and after all six are lit the Jetways settle at 250K apiece for the rest of the ball.

goals.title: Arm The Magnet
goals.summary: The Magnet is the difference between the Wall being hard and being free. Shoot the Pit while its Magnet lamp is lit, and the ball gets pinned right at the upper right flipper's tip. Wait for the count-down and the call to flip — go early and it releases immediately, wait too long and you lose it too.
goals.reward: A free shot at the Wall

steps.action: Shoot the Pit with the Magnet lamp lit
steps.detail: The Pit is reachable from either lower flipper.
The countdown runs while the ball travels the habitrail; flipping before the ball settles kills the magnet outright.
One shot only — the Magnet switches off after it.

goals.title: Complete S-K-A-T-E
goals.summary: The five standups on the left wall. Clearing them lights a WILLIAMS letter and relights the Magnet, which makes this the most useful repeat task on the machine. Learn where on the bank a right-flipper shot rebounds into the Pit and you can do two jobs with one swing.
goals.reward: A WILLIAMS letter and a relit Magnet

steps.detail: Flashing means not yet hit; steady means collected.
There is a point on the bank, different on every machine, where the ball kicks back into the Pit.
Completing the bank relights the Magnet at the Pit.

goals.title: Roller Motion
goals.summary: A near-random award collected at the Pit. The pool runs from nothing at all through Jetter Bonus, Bonus Held, a WILLIAMS letter, Spot Team, Bonus X, Extra Ball and Lite Special. Instant Lock is the one to hope for — it gives you a lock and relights the Magnet at once.
goals.reward: Anything from zero to an extra ball

steps.detail: Roller Motion is lit at game start but not at the start of each ball — the center standups are what bring it back.

steps.action: Let the bumpers do the work
steps.detail: Those standups are nearly unshootable directly; balls knocked around the bumpers hit them for you.
Roller Motion cannot be collected during multiball.

goals.title: The Scoring Cycle
goals.summary: Spell WILLIAMS and a hurry-up starts at four million and falls to one. You collect it at the Pit. The countdown holds for a beat before it begins, which makes a full four million possible but very tight. Miss it entirely and you drop back four letters rather than losing the lot.

steps.detail: The sequence carries over between balls, players and even games.
Collecting resets WILLIAMS completely; failing to collect only rolls it back four letters.
The best shot at the full four million is finishing the letter off the S-K-A-T-E bank so the same ball rebounds straight into the Pit.

goals.title: Shooting The Wall
goals.summary: Every big award on this machine collects at the Wall, and three arrow lamps tell you which one is live: red for Jackpot, green for Lock, orange for Million. It is only reachable from the upper right flipper, which is why the Magnet matters so much.
goals.reward: Jackpot, Lock or Million depending on the lamp

steps.action: Get the ball to the upper flipper
steps.detail: The Pit habitrail, the kickback and the bumpers all deliver it there.

steps.action: Check the arrows before you shoot
steps.detail: With both Million and Lock lit the ball may or may not be diverted into the lock, so the same shot can pay differently.
A ball that falls out the left exit or back down the entrance awards no lock, but Lock stays lit for the next attempt.

goals.title: The Double-Dip Shot
goals.summary: The switch that registers a Wall shot sits on the upslope, below the flat section at the top. A ball that is hit just hard enough to trip the switch, stall, and roll back down over it earns two awards from one shot. Deliberately underhitting the Wall is a real technique here.
goals.reward: Two Wall awards from one shot

steps.action: Aim to stall it on the slope
steps.detail: Too hard and it clears the diverters; too soft and it never reaches the switch.
The ball comes back down at the upper right flipper for another attempt.

steps.action: Use it on Locks and Millions
steps.detail: Two credited shots means two chances at whatever the arrows have lit.

goals.title: Lock Three And Go
goals.summary: The W-A-R drop targets award locks in single-ball play, and three locked balls starts multiball. When it fires, all three come down the right inlane together, which is unpleasant. The Magnet is armed automatically at the start, so you get one free crack at the first jackpot.

steps.detail: They can be taken from any flipper, and the upper right flipper can sweep the whole bank.
It is worth between one and a half and four million, and it is the only one worth real money — every collection resets it to 1.5M.
All the locked balls arrive down the right inlane at once; normal play resumes once you are down to one.

goals.title: Bank Targets In Multiball
goals.summary: Because the jackpot resets to a million and a half every time you collect it, the target completions are often the better money. Completing S-K-A-T-E during multiball pays 100K, then 150K, then 200K and upward to a half million ceiling. W-A-R pays on the same ladder.

steps.detail: The bank resets after multiball ends anyway, so there is nothing to save.
Both banks run their own separate climbing ladder.
Get the big one out of the way, then farm the banks while balls are alive.

goals.title: Sudden Death
goals.summary: This starts on its own during single-ball play, once or twice a game. Fifteen seconds on the clock, and every Wall shot pays a million and resets the timer. Complete both S-K-A-T-E and W-A-R and the round ends with a two million bonus.

steps.detail: Every hit buys another fifteen seconds, so the round can run a long time.

steps.action: Or close it out for the bonus
steps.detail: Completing both banks ends the round with two million.
Repeated Wall shots can outscore the two million, but the round has also been seen to end after five or six quick ramp hits.

goals.title: The Combo Shot
goals.summary: Left Jetway into the Wall pays 100K the first time and another 100K each time after, up to a half million ceiling. The Jetway does not need to be lit, and the combo pays on top of whatever the Wall was already going to give you.

steps.detail: Lit or unlit, either works as the first half.
Only the combo display shows, but you are paid for both.
The value climbs a hundred thousand each time until it caps.

goals.title: Power Plays
goals.summary: Hit the Wall when nothing is lit and you bank a Power Play. Three of them lights an extra ball and eight lights the outlane Specials. They carry for the whole game, which makes an unlit Wall shot far from wasted.
goals.reward: Extra ball at three, Specials at eight

steps.action: Shoot it even with nothing lit
steps.detail: A Combo Shot does not stop a Power Play being awarded.
Extra balls stack at the Center Lane and stay lit until you take them.
The counts are operator-adjustable but three and eight are the usual settings.

goals.title: Keep The Kickback Alive
goals.summary: The left outlane kickback is unusual — instead of dropping the ball back on the flipper, it fires it up a ramp onto a second kicker and around the orbit to the upper right flipper. So a save here hands you a Wall shot. The A-B-C standups relight it.
goals.reward: A saved ball delivered to the upper flipper

steps.detail: Three targets low on the right, angled toward the lower left flipper.
Relight it before you need it — the divider on this side gives you almost nothing to nudge against.
The saved ball arrives at the upper right flipper, so have a Wall shot in mind.

goals.title: J-E-T Bonus Multiplier
goals.summary: The three lanes above the bumpers advance the bonus multiplier up to seven times. They are hard to hit deliberately because the orbit passes above them with no gate, so lane-change with the flipper buttons whenever a ball is heading up there.
goals.reward: Up to 7x bonus, then 100K per completion

steps.detail: Either flipper button shifts them right; do it while the ball is still travelling.
Most lane completions come from balls popping back up out of the nest rather than from aimed shots.

steps.action: Or take Bonus X from the Pit
steps.detail: Roller Motion has Bonus X in its award pool. Note the lanes do not carry between balls.

goals.title: The Center Lane
goals.summary: A lane so narrow it looks impossible. Send the ball straight up the middle, clearing the drop targets on one side and the ramp entrance on the other, then slipping past the center standups with the bumpers alongside. It is the only place extra balls are collected, and any you light wait there indefinitely, so an unclaimed one is never lost.
goals.reward: Every extra ball in the game

steps.detail: No angle will do it — the shot has to leave the flipper on a dead vertical line.
Come down the J lane and the bumpers will sometimes bat the ball into it for you.
Every extra ball you light waits here for you and they pile up, so there is no rush.

goals.title: Outlane Specials
goals.summary: A Lite Special award from Roller Motion, or eight Power Plays, lights both outlanes at once. They stay lit until one is hit — and then both go out together, so you only get one Special per lighting.

steps.action: Draw Lite Special from Roller Motion
steps.detail: It sits in the same random pool as Extra Ball and Instant Lock.
Power Plays carry all game, so this is the route you can plan for.
Both light and both die on the first collection.

achievements.title: Both Jetways
achievements.desc: Light both Jetways and collect them with a single orbit shot.

achievements.title: Don't Flip
achievements.desc: Arm the Magnet at the Pit and hold your nerve until the call to flip.

achievements.title: Jetway Into The Wall
achievements.desc: Complete the Combo Shot from the left Jetway into the ramp.

achievements.title: Six Teams
achievements.desc: Light all six Rollergames teams in a single ball.

achievements.title: Three In The Lock
achievements.desc: Lock three balls off the W-A-R drops and start multiball.

achievements.title: Sudden Death
achievements.desc: Keep resetting the Sudden Death timer with repeated Wall shots.

achievements.title: Two For One
achievements.desc: Stall a ball on the Wall so it credits the ramp switch twice.

achievements.title: Full Four Million
achievements.desc: Complete WILLIAMS and collect the Scoring Cycle before the value starts falling.

achievements.title: Threading The Needle
achievements.desc: Hit the Center Lane on purpose and collect a lit extra ball.

achievements.title: Eight Power Plays
achievements.desc: Bank eight Power Plays in one game to light the outlane Specials.

drills.title: Plunge Into The Wall
drills.text: A full-strength plunge sends the ball straight up the Wall, so read the three arrow lamps before you launch and know what that shot is going to pay. Do not plan a lock off it — the game refuses to count one from the plunger, so the plunge Wall shot is points, not progress.
drills.reps: every ball start, one full game

drills.title: Hands Still For The Magnet
drills.text: Shoot the Pit with the Magnet lamp lit and then keep your hands off the buttons — the countdown runs while the ball travels the habitrail, and flipping before it settles kills the magnet outright. Wait for the call, flip once, and the Wall stops being a difficult shot.

drills.title: Find The Rebound Spot
drills.text: Clear the flashing S-K-A-T-E targets off the right flipper and hunt for the point on the bank where the ball kicks back into the Pit — it sits in a different place on every machine, so find it on the one in front of you. Completing the bank relights the Magnet at the Pit, so the right rebound does both jobs in one swing.
drills.reps: until you can hit the rebound spot on demand

drills.title: Both Jetways, One Orbit
drills.text: Left inlane lights the right Jetway and right inlane lights the left one, and both can be lit at once — so bank a ball that has crossed both inlanes and take a single full orbit to collect the pair. Only the spinner has to trip, not the whole orbit, so a shot that dies partway round still pays.
drills.reps: light all six teams inside one ball

drills.title: Stall It On The Slope
drills.text: The switch that registers a Wall shot sits on the upslope below the flat top, so a ball hit just hard enough to trip it, stall, and roll back over it pays twice. Underhitting the Wall on purpose is a real technique here — work the strength from the upper right flipper until you can stall it deliberately rather than by accident.

drills.title: Jetway Into The Wall
drills.text: Left Jetway straight into the Wall is a combo whether the Jetway is lit or not, and it pays on top of whatever the Wall was already going to give you. Run it on repeat — the value climbs every time until it caps, and an unlit Wall shot still banks a Power Play.

actionButton.how: A 1990 Williams front panel: manual plunger, flippers, start button, nothing more. The only button habit worth building is lane change — either flipper button rotates the lit J-E-T lanes, and since the orbit passes above them with no gate you will rarely hit them on purpose, so do the rotating while the ball is still travelling.

howItPlays.objective: Roller Games spins a roller-derby broadcast into a chase up the near-vertical Wall, the one shot that pays every jackpot, lock and million. Skate all six teams into the lineup by banking Jetways, pin the ball with the Magnet so that brutal Wall becomes a gimme, and stash three balls for multiball.
loop: Roll a return lane to arm the Jetway on the far side of the table, then clip its spinner to bank it and drop one of your team lamps into place.
Rake the left-wall standups clean to earn a WILLIAMS letter and flip the Magnet back on over at the Pit.
Feed the Pit while the Magnet glows, keep both thumbs off the buttons, and let it clamp the ball at the upper flipper for a free run at the Wall.
Glance at the Wall's three colored arrows and shoot the upper flipper for whichever award is live; a dark Wall shot still pockets a Power Play.
Stack three locks on the W-A-R drops to tip into multiball, then harvest both standup banks over and over while the balls are loose.

lights.name: Jetway Spinners
lights.lit: An orange Jetway lamp glows at a spinner's mouth the moment the return lane on the far side arms it, and nothing stops both mouths burning together; the spinner switch by itself is the collect, so an orbit that stalls partway round still pays.
lights.then: Each Jetway you take drops one of your six team lamps onto the bare centre of the table, and lighting the whole crew opens an extra ball down the tight Center Lane. A drain wipes the lamps, so the set has to land on one ball -- once it does, every Jetway flattens to a quarter-million apiece.

lights.name: S-K-A-T-E Standups
lights.lit: A standup on the left wall burns steady once you have knocked it down and holds for the rest of the ball; the ones still blinking are the letters you owe.
lights.flashing: A blinking target is a letter you have not collected yet.
lights.then: Finishing the bank hands you a WILLIAMS letter and snaps the Magnet back on at the Pit in one motion. There is a rebound point on this wall where a right-flipper shot ricochets straight into the Pit, so one swing does both jobs; bank the full WILLIAMS to arm a hurry-up worth as much as four million.

lights.name: W-A-R Drop Targets
lights.lit: Each of the three drops wears a lamp showing whether that lock is banked, still open, or open but ticking down on a timer; any flipper can reach the row, and the upper one can rake the whole set in a single pass.
lights.then: Award a lock on all three and you tip into multiball, where the balls spill down the right inlane in one rush as it begins. The Magnet arms itself the instant it starts, handing you one clean crack at that opening jackpot before the noise takes over.

lights.name: The Wall Arrows
lights.lit: Three arrow lamps at the ramp mouth tell you what a Wall shot pays right now -- red for a jackpot, green for a lock, orange for a million -- and only the upper right flipper can fire it, which is exactly why the Magnet earns its keep.
lights.then: Send it from the upper flipper for whatever the arrows have lit; with none of them lit the shot still banks a Power Play, and those pile up all game toward an extra ball at three and lit outlane Specials at eight. Underhit it so it stalls on the ramp switch and rolls back over, and a single shot credits twice.

lights.name: The Magnet
lights.lit: A lit Magnet lamp at the Pit means the grabber out on the upper flipper's tip is live; feed the Pit and the ball is carried up the rail and held dead still right where you want it for the Wall.
lights.then: While the ball rides the wire a countdown ticks -- touch a button early and the grabber lets go at once, sit too long and it drops anyway, so wait for the call and flip a single time for a gift Wall shot. It switches off after that one shot; clearing the left-wall standups is the fastest way to bring it back.

lights.name: J-E-T Rollover Lanes
lights.lit: The trio of lanes over the bumpers lights toward your bonus multiplier; a lane already collected stays lit, and the dark ones are all you have left to sweep.

control.effect: either flipper button nudges the lit lanes across by one step, so you can park a lit lane under whatever path the ball is taking -- the orbit sails over this trio with no gate to stop it, so you almost never aim these and instead steer the lit ones under a ball already on its way
control.when: while the ball is still climbing up toward the lanes

lights.then: Complete all three to step the bonus multiplier up a rung at a time, to a ceiling of seven; past that, each completion is a flat hundred thousand. The lit lanes do not carry between balls, so you rebuild them from scratch every ball.

lights.name: Roller Motion
lights.lit: With the Roller Motion lamp lit at the Pit, a trip inside draws a random award off a wheel that ranges from an outright blank up through a held bonus, a spotted team, a multiplier bump, an extra ball, a lit Special, and the prize you actually want -- an instant lock that relights the Magnet at the same time.
lights.then: Bring the award back by knocking the 1-2-3 standups buried among the bumpers -- almost impossible to shoot on purpose, so let the nest bat the ball into them for you -- then collect at the Pit. It sits out during multiball, so cash it while a single ball is in play.

howItPlays.laneChangeNote: Either flipper button nudges the lit J-E-T lanes across by one, so tap it while the ball is still climbing toward them to seat a lit lane in the ball's path -- the orbit runs over the trio with no gate, which makes steering the lit ones far more reliable than aiming for them. Sweeping the set steps your bonus multiplier up to a ceiling of seven, then pays a flat hundred thousand for each completion after.

scoring.text: Lean on the safe, repeatable points first: cross the return lanes to arm the Jetways and clip the spinners to spot teams, and rake the left-wall standups to stock WILLIAMS letters while keeping the Magnet lit. Finish the A-B-C standups early to re-arm the left kickback, because the thin divider on that rail leaves you next to nothing to lean on.

Set the Magnet at the Pit for a free swing at the Wall, and read the arrows so you know what each swing is worth. Bank a Power Play every time the Wall is dark, climbing toward the extra ball, and stack three locks off the W-A-R drops to open multiball -- then farm both standup banks up their climbing ladders while the balls last.

There is no wizard mode here -- the peak of the game is Locks Multiball, opened by stashing three balls off the drops, where the auto-armed Magnet hands you a first jackpot as large as four million before it resets low. The other big night is the WILLIAMS hurry-up cashed at the Pit, and Sudden Death, which starts on its own and pays a million for every Wall shot as its clock keeps resetting.
